newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European shares slip as Wall Street stumbles.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European shares slip as Wall Street stumbles.

text.p: Leading European share markets slipped on Thursday after Wall Street's three-day comeback came to an abrupt halt overnight.
On the foreign exchange markets, the dollar retreated from a 55-month high against the yen as traders became increasingly nervous about possible Japanese intervention.
It also slipped against the mark although German officials, unlike their Japanese counterparts, have been conspicuously silent in recent days during the dollar surge.

New York dictated the trend on European equities as the U.S. rally, which followed last week's 215-point tumble, reversed after European dealers went home on Wednesday. The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed down 45.32 points (0.69 percent) at 6,563.84.
But the European losses were modest, falling short in percentage terms of the Wall Street drop. London was the least affected, with the FTSE 100 down just 0.3 of a point at 4,292.0 at mid morning.
"There's precious little selling and the buyers come and go," said one London dealer.

London investors had reasons of their own to sit on the fence. Campaigning for the May 1 general election, where the ruling Conservatives are struggling to narrow the Labour party's big opinion poll lead, injected the usual dose of uncertainty.
Also finance minister Kenneth Clarke is due to hold his last monthly meeting with Bank of England Governor Eddie George before the election on Thursday at 1415 GMT.

Analysts believe an unpopular interest rate rise, which most believe is needed to nip inflation in the bud, would come after the polls rather than before, whoever wins. "The consensus is that they won't raise rates before the election although there's a sneaking feeling that the Conservatives think it might look dynamic and positive to do so," said one dealer.
The Bank of France is also holding a policy meeting on Thursday and investors haboured hopes of of a slight fall in interest rates.
One operator said the central bank could cut by five basis points. "It's unlikely. But why not? It wouldn't be out of sight. It would boost the market," he said.
Nevertheless, the market consolidated after Wednesday's gains and the CAC-40 was down 6.25 points or 0.24 percent at 2,611.30.
Wall Street likewise pulled down the German market, with the DAX index down 15.71 points or 0.47 percent at 3,343.75. Dealers also blamed the weakening of the dollar against the mark.
German industry had benefited from the mark's weakness in recent months against the dollar and sterling, which has tracked the U.S. currency more than its European counterparts.

A major German exporter, carmaker Volkswagen, gave evidence of this on Thursday. Chief financial officer Bruno Adelt said the mark's weakening boosted 1996 earnings by about 600 million marks ($350 million) and he expected 1997 profits also to benefit.
The dollar backed away on Thursday from the 55-month high overnight against the yen with dealers still jittery about the possibility of Bank of Japan intervention.

It was at 126.08 yen compared with the overnight high of 127.16 and Wednesday's European close of 126.83. It also edged down from a 37-month high of 1.7272 marks to 1.7152 compared with the previous close of 1.7250.
"The fact that the Bundesbank has not even attempted to slow the dollar's rise through some verbal intervention ... is increasingly drawing attention," said Klaus Baader of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Later Bundesbank Council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher did break that silence, saying: "We do not need to strengthen the mark."

But the state sceretary at the German finance ministry, Juergen Stark, also said a dollar/mark exchange rate over 1.72 was part of a normal market correction. Stark's comments helped to lift the mark a little.
Japanese authorities have recently started to become quite vocal on the dollar's rise.
Senior Finance Ministry offical Eisuke Sakakibara said overnight that intervention was possible if foreign exchange rates deviated from fundamentals.
Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka also said Japan would act decisively with excessive currency movements. But dealers saw no sign of central bank activity.
CURRENCIES AT 0900 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.7152 marks and 126.08 yen, compared to 1.7250 and 126.83 in late European trade on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0900 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 0.3 points at 4,292.0.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 15.71 points
PARIS - The CAC-40 index was 6.25 points lower at 2,611.30.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 0900 GMT
Gold was at $348.50 an ounce, compared with the London close of $347.95 on Wednesday. Silver was unchanged at $4.79.
